# Large response atoms pay by an actual convex hinge

This note supplies a precise elementary filter for the unbuffered
outward-smoothed problem. It does not assert that a suitable large atom
exists in every source menu.

Work in the attained compact minimal-bad-body class at a fixed h>0.
At source i select a response menu nu_i on its active caps:
sum_j nu_ij=1 and sum_j nu_ij S_ij u_ij=0. The active cap j has
margin l_ij(w)=N_ij.w-c_ij, width h Gamma(u_ij), and profile
W_ij(w)=Psi(l_ij(w)/(h Gamma(u_ij))). Normalize Gamma(u_ij)=1.

## One large atom

Suppose nu_ij=w_i>0. The field

    Phi_i(n,z,x)=[l_ij(z,x)]_+

is finite, nonnegative, continuous, and convex in all physical coordinates.
It is independent of the boundary normal n and is therefore an admissible
convex physical field. Its boundary integral D_i is strictly positive:
the selected cap cuts the source's own uniform interior ball properly,
and a nonempty open portion of the own boundary has positive margin.
All fibers are bounded, so D_i is finite. Replace Phi_i by Phi_i/D_i.

On the support of this normalized field the chosen cap has profile
identically one. Every other cap profile is nonnegative. Consequently

    integral_boundary Phi_i sum_j nu_ij W_ij >= w_i.       (1)

No inference from a volume fraction to a boundary fraction is used:
the identity follows pointwise from the positive-margin hinge.

## Simultaneous descent for all sources

Choose one such menu and normalized field for each of the k deepest
sources, and put Phi=sum_i Phi_i. This is one actual admissible field
and has total boundary integral k. For each source i, nonnegativity of
all cross captures and (1) give

    integral_boundary Phi sum_j nu_ij W_ij >= w_i.

The exact unbuffered source loss for this menu is

    integral W_i Phi + sum_j nu_ij A_ij (D-J_ij)/(2M).

The term sum nu_ij(-A_ij)J_ij/(2M) is nonnegative. On the compact class
0<=-A_ij<=h S_max, so the remaining constant loss is bounded below by
-h S_max D/(2M). Thus the normalized improvement of EVERY group is at least

    w_i - k [beta_h+h S_max/(2M)].                       (2)

If min_i w_i >= Gamma_d, then (2) is positive whenever
beta_h+h S_max/(2M)<Gamma_d/k. Exact frozen-menu covering then gives a
strict decrease of the actual body objective, contradicting minimality.
Since k<=k(P)<=2^n and M is normalized to one, this excludes a strict
below-OC minimizing sequence whenever every source admits such a menu.

This implication uses the complete menu choice before separation. It
does not assume that a separator selected for another menu is unchanged.

## Minimal circuits

A maximizing response menu can be chosen extreme, supported on at most
d+1 caps. Its positive support is a minimal positive linear circuit:
if the vectors S_j u_j had a second independent linear dependence, a
small signed weight perturbation would preserve total mass and balance,
contradicting extremality after restriction to its support. More directly,
an extreme probability with k positive atoms has rank k-1 in these
vectors, with its positive dependence spanning the one-dimensional
kernel. Rescaling by S_j>0 gives the same circuit property for u_j.

A rank-one circuit has exactly two oppositely directed continuous
normals. One of its RESPONSE weights is at least 1/2, hence at least
Gamma_d for every d>=1. The preceding hinge argument pays such a source,
irrespective of its base tilts and all oblique ambient orientations.

For rank at least two a minimal positive circuit has neither repeated
nor antipodal continuous directions: either would give a nontrivial
proper subcircuit or a linear dependence supported on a proper subset.
Consequently at most one cap in such a menu can support a given
positive-area fiber facet. Different source menus may still support the
same facet, and this observation does not remove that overlap.

The remaining best-menu efficiency question is therefore concentrated
on source menus with at least three atoms and without any response
weight as large as Gamma_d. Neither these properties nor the circuit
description imply the missing sharp payment.
